newsitem.title: USA: IMF executive board to meet on Uganda debt plan.
newsitem.headline: IMF executive board to meet on Uganda debt plan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund executive board meets on Wednesday to discuss a plan to help Uganda reduce its debt load to managable levels, officials said Tuesday, in a first case of new program for very poor countries.

The IMF meeting follows discussions on Monday at the World Bank, where it was generally agreed that the country should be provided up to about $385 million under the debt initiative for heavily indebted poor countries, according to monetary sources.
The discussions and any formal agreement that comes from them is being closely watched by developing countries since it could set the pattern for any future assistance under the new debt initiative.

The intent is to face the reality that poor countries carrying huge debts, including repayments to international institutions designed to help them such as the Bank and IMF, need foregiveness to debt levels that they can handle.

But the plan has not been without controversy and there has been no firm agreement on when the money should be provided Uganda, although both the IMF and Bank agree the country has worked hard to reform its economy.
In general, a country is required under the initiative to establish a six year record with IMF tutorship that shows strong economic reform efforts.

The debate over Uganda involves when the debt relief should take place with the the Britain favoring this Fall and the United States, in a controversial stance, recommending April 1999, according to the sources.

Other countries in line to possibly take advantage of the program are Bolivia, Mozambique and Burkina Faso, although they may face more difficult hurdles since they may not be as far along the reform path.
